questions.hint: Divide the force by the acceleration.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: Which of these transformations does NOT always preserve the solution set of an equation?

options.text: Dividing both sides by x, because x might be zero
Adding 2 to both sides, because constants change the balance
options.misconception: believes adding the same constant changes solutions

options.text: Multiplying both sides by 3, because scaling changes the value of x
options.misconception: thinks multiplying by a nonzero number changes solutions

options.text: Subtracting x from both sides, because the variable disappears
options.misconception: believes moving a variable term removes solutions

questions.explanation: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing both sides by the same nonzero quantity preserves solutions. Dividing by a variable is not always valid because the variable may be zero. The trap is confusing reversible operations with conditional ones.
questions.hint: Ask whether the divisor could be zero.

questions.stem: Solve 7x plus 2 equals 3x plus 18. What is x? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Subtracting 3x gives 4x plus 2 equals 18, then subtracting 2 gives 4x equals 16, so x equals 4. Checking gives 30 on both sides. Moving the variable to the side with the larger coefficient keeps the arithmetic simple.
questions.hint: Subtract the smaller variable term first.

questions.stem: Solve y equals (3/7)x plus 2 for x. If y equals 11, what is x? Report the number only.

questions.hint: Subtract 2 first, then multiply by the reciprocal of 3/7.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: A bottle holds 0.75 litres. Given 1 litre equals 1000 millilitres, which equation finds the volume v in millilitres?

options.text: v equals 0.75 times 1000, because millilitres are smaller than litres
v equals 0.75 divided by 1000, because conversion always divides
options.misconception: divides instead of multiplying for a smaller unit

options.text: v equals 0.75 plus 1000, because the factor is added
options.misconception: adds the conversion factor

options.text: v equals 1000 divided by 0.75, because the units are inverted
options.misconception: inverts the quantity and the factor

questions.explanation: Since millilitres are smaller, the count increases: 0.75 litres times 1000 millilitres per litre gives 750 millilitres. Dividing would give a fraction of a litre.
questions.hint: Multiply because the new unit is smaller.

questions.stem: A student answers 64 percent of 25 questions correctly. Which equation finds the number correct c?

options.text: c equals 0.64 times 25, because the percent of the total is the part correct
c equals 64 times 25, because the percent is used as a whole number
options.misconception: uses the percent as a whole number multiplier

options.text: c equals 25 divided by 0.64, because the count is found by sharing
options.misconception: divides by the percent

options.text: c equals 25 minus 64, because the percent is subtracted
options.misconception: subtracts the percent from the total

questions.explanation: Sixty-four percent means 0.64, so the number correct is 0.64 times 25, which is 16. Using 64 as a multiplier gives a count above the total.
questions.hint: Convert 64 percent to 0.64 before multiplying.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: A pharmacist mixes 9 litres of 10 percent solution with x litres of 30 percent solution to get a 20 percent mixture. Which equation balances the solute?

options.text: 0.10 times 9 plus 0.30 times x equals 0.20 times (9 plus x), because solute before equals solute after
0.10 plus 0.30 equals 0.20 times x, because concentrations add directly
options.misconception: adds concentrations without weighting by volume

options.text: 9 plus x equals 0.20 times 0.10, because total volume equals a percent of concentration
options.misconception: confuses total volume with solute amount

options.text: 0.10 times 9 equals 0.30 times x, because the two solute amounts must match
options.misconception: forces the two contributions to be equal

questions.explanation: Solute from each part is concentration times volume, and the final solute is 0.20 times the total volume. Equating those balances the mixture. Adding concentrations or forcing equality ignores the volumes.
questions.hint: Multiply each concentration by its volume before adding.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: A train travels at 80 kilometres per hour. Which equation finds the time t in hours to travel 320 kilometres?

options.text: 80 times t equals 320, because speed times time equals distance
80 plus t equals 320, because speed and time add to distance
options.misconception: adds speed and time

options.text: t equals 80 divided by 320, because time is speed over distance
options.misconception: inverts speed and distance

options.text: 80 times 320 equals t, because distance times speed gives time
options.misconception: multiplies distance by speed

questions.explanation: Speed times time equals distance, so 80 times t equals 320. Solving gives t equals 4 hours. Adding or inverting does not produce a distance.
questions.hint: Match units: kilometres per hour times hours gives kilometres.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: Grace is 9 years older than Mia. In 7 years Grace will be 4 times as old as Mia is now. Which equation finds Mia's current age m?

options.text: m plus 9 plus 7 equals 4 times m, because Grace's future age equals 4 times Mia's current age
m plus 9 equals 4 times (m plus 7), because Mia's future age is quadrupled
options.misconception: quadruples the wrong person's age

options.text: m plus 7 equals 4 times (m plus 9), because the age gap is quadrupled
options.misconception: quadruples Grace's current age instead

options.text: m plus 16 equals 4 times m, because the gap grows by 7
options.misconception: adds the time to the age gap

questions.explanation: Grace's current age is m plus 9, and in 7 years it is m plus 16, which equals 4 times m. The trap is quadrupling the wrong age or misplacing the 7 years.
questions.hint: Add 7 to Grace's current age m plus 9.

questions.stem: The line is y equals 2x plus 3. Which point lies on it?

(1, 2), because 2 times 1 is 2 and the plus 3 is dropped
options.misconception: drops the constant

options.text: (2, 5), because 2 times 2 plus 3 is computed as 5
options.misconception: miscalculates 4 plus 3 as 5

options.text: (0, 2), because the slope is read as the intercept
options.misconception: swaps slope and intercept

questions.explanation: Substituting x equals 1 gives 2 plus 3, which is 5, matching the y coordinate. The other points fail the substitution test. Dropping the constant or mishandling its value are common slips.

questions.stem: A student rearranges y equals 5x minus 4 to x equals (y plus 4) divided by 5. She tests x equals 3. Which result shows the rearrangement is correct?

options.text: Original gives y equals 11, rearranged gives 3 equals (11 plus 4) divided by 5, which is 3, so it checks
Original gives y equals 11, rearranged gives 3 equals (11 minus 4) divided by 5, which fails
options.misconception: uses minus 4 instead of plus 4

options.text: Original gives y equals 19, rearranged gives 3 equals (19 plus 4) divided by 5, which fails
options.misconception: computes 5 times 3 minus 4 as 19

options.text: Original gives y equals 11, rearranged gives 3 equals (11 plus 4) times 5, which fails
options.misconception: multiplies instead of dividing

questions.explanation: With x equals 3 the original gives y equals 5 times 3 minus 4, which is 11. The rearranged form gives (11 plus 4) divided by 5, which is 3. The pair satisfies both forms, so the rearrangement is correct.
questions.hint: Generate y from the original, then evaluate the rearranged form.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.stem: Two lines on a graph intersect at exactly one point. What does that tell you about the system?

options.text: The system has exactly one solution, because the lines meet once
The system has no solution, because the lines are not parallel
options.misconception: confuses non-parallel with parallel

options.text: The system has infinitely many solutions, because the lines cross
options.misconception: confuses crossing with overlapping

options.text: The system has two solutions, one for each line
options.misconception: counts individual line solutions

questions.explanation: Lines that intersect at one point share exactly that point, so the system has one solution. Infinitely many solutions would require the lines to coincide completely.
questions.hint: A single crossing point gives a single solution pair.

questions.subject: ALGEBRA_I
questions.learningObjective: identify a no-solution system from standard form
questions.stem: The system is 4x plus 6y equals 8 and 2x plus 3y equals 5. How many solutions does it have?

options.text: None, because the second left side is half the first but the constant is not
Infinitely many, because the coefficients are proportional
options.misconception: ignores that the constant must also be proportional

options.text: Exactly one, because there are two equations
options.misconception: assumes two equations always give one solution

options.text: Exactly two, one for each equation
options.misconception: counts individual equation solutions

questions.explanation: The left side of the second equation is half the first, but the right side 5 is not half of 8. That gives parallel distinct lines with no common point. Proportional coefficients alone are not enough; the constant must scale by the same factor.
questions.hint: Check whether the constant also halves.
